key_insight: A training-free, attribution-guided correction (BAMI) can identify and mitigate two main sources of GUI grounding errors—precision bias from high-resolution screens and ambiguity bias from complex UI elements—improving localization at inference time without retraining.
problem_solved: Existing GUI grounding models underperform on complex, high-resolution interfaces (e.g., ScreenSpot-Pro) because they are biased toward imprecise localization and confused by visually intricate or ambiguous UI components.
method: Use Masked Prediction Distribution (MPD) attribution to diagnose per-input error sources and separate precision vs. ambiguity biases.

Apply BAMI at inference time (training-free): resolution-aware masking and multi-scale aggregation to reduce precision bias, plus ambiguity-aware candidate re-ranking/thresholding to disambiguate complex elements.
Operate entirely at inference without modifying model weights or requiring extra labeled data, making mitigation lightweight and pluggable.
impact: Enables more reliable GUI agents and faster deployment by fixing common grounding failure modes without costly retraining or dataset expansion, lowering the barrier for robust human–computer interaction models.

paper_title: BAMI: Training-Free Bias Mitigation in GUI Grounding
paper_authors: Borui Zhang, Bo Zhang, Bo Wang, Wenzhao Zheng, Yuhao Cheng
